- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.30) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent highs — model often overreacts to short-term momentum.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged correction: if true outcome is significantly below forecast, adjust next period’s forecast downward by 2–5% to account for momentum decay.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment spikes — sentiment should be weighted less than 50% for long-term forecasts.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should not forecast >+15% above prior peak — avoid “over-optimism” bias.
